summary: 11 concrete, comment-endorsed tools and learning products selected from a verified 30-story HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: turbo-fieldfare
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Open-source engine running Gemma 4 26B in 2 GB RAM on any M-series Mac
items.summary: An open-source Mac engine that streams Gemma 4 experts from storage to minimize RAM use.
items.why_included: A firsthand benchmark reported fast, graceful performance under memory pressure on an M4 Max.
items.evidence: A commenter benchmarked turbo-fieldfare on a 64 GB M4 Max and praised its gradual degradation under memory pressure.

evidence_sources.author: pwython
evidence_sources.excerpt: Ran this on a 64 GB M4 Max MacBook.

items.name: Hacker News Button
items.source_story_title: Show HN: I was tired of opening 2 tabs for every HN link, so I made a userscript
items.summary: A Firefox extension that finds Hacker News discussions for the page currently being read.
items.why_included: It offers an explicitly privacy-conscious alternative that avoids a request until the button is pressed.
items.evidence: Its creator said the extension uses Bloom filters and makes no external request unless the user presses the button.

evidence_sources.author: jstrieb
evidence_sources.excerpt: Using Bloom filters means that there are no external requests unless you actually press the button.

items.name: BookOrbit
items.summary: A self-hostable book-library service with KOReader sync for progress and annotations.
items.why_included: A long-term Kindle user described it as part of their preferred open, self-hosted reading setup.
items.evidence: A commenter said BookOrbit provides a KOReader plugin that syncs reading progress and annotations.

evidence_sources.author: joshstrange
evidence_sources.excerpt: BookOrbit: It provides a plugin for KOReader that syncs your progress, annotations, etc.

items.name: Murasaki
items.summary: A lightweight macOS reader for EPUB and PDF files.
items.why_included: It was enthusiastically recommended for performance and a focused reading experience.
items.evidence: A commenter called Murasaki the most performant and sleek macOS ebook reader they had found.

evidence_sources.author: carlosjobim
evidence_sources.excerpt: Murasaki [1] is the most performant and sleek ebook reader you can get for MacOS currently.

items.name: Librera
items.source_story_title: More Tailscale tricks for your jailbroken Kindle
items.summary: An Android ebook reader available in a full version through F-Droid.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended as a strong Android alternative for configurable reading.
items.evidence: A commenter called Librera a similarly awesome ebook reader on Android and noted that F-Droid carries the full version.

evidence_sources.author: dizhn
evidence_sources.excerpt: A similarly awesome ebook reader on Android is Librera.

items.name: Picotron
items.source_story_title: User Interfaces of the Demo Scene
items.summary: A fantasy workstation for making and sharing small software, music, and visual tools.
items.why_included: It was strongly recommended for preserving the expressive, custom-UI spirit of demoscene tools.
items.evidence: A commenter strongly recommended Picotron for its nostalgic interface, music tracker, and ecosystem of custom utilities.

evidence_sources.author: aquova
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you're interested or nostalgic for these types of UIs, I would strongly recommend Picotron[0].

items.name: RapidRAW
items.summary: An open-source RAW photo editor with frequent releases and an active maintainer.
items.why_included: A longtime Darktable user reported moving to it after repeated workflow and camera-color problems.
items.evidence: A commenter said they were starting to love RapidRAW and highlighted its active development cadence.

evidence_sources.author: qurren
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'm currently starting to love RapidRAW

items.name: Math Academy
items.source_story_title: LearnVector – Andrew Ng's AI company building one‑to‑one learning experiences
items.summary: An adaptive math-learning platform centered on structured practice and progress tracking.
items.why_included: A new user signed up after an HN recommendation and called it exactly what they wanted.
items.evidence: A commenter said they signed up for Math Academy after a quick look and found it fantastic.

evidence_sources.author: Douger
evidence_sources.excerpt: After a quick look I signed up and it is fantastic - exactly what I wanted.

items.name: Socratic Quiz skill
items.source_story_title: LearnVector – Andrew Ng's AI company building one‑to‑one learning experiences
items.summary: A Claude skill that tutors through document-led Socratic questions rather than immediate answers.
items.why_included: A user reported that it worked well for learning from dense linear-algebra and Postgres material.
items.evidence: A commenter called the Socratic-method skill fantastic after using it with dense technical PDFs.

evidence_sources.author: genghisjahn
evidence_sources.excerpt: I’ve found this to be fantastic.

items.name: Hubble
items.source_story_title: Hubble: Open-source notetaking app for you and your agents
items.summary: A local Markdown note app designed for shared use by people and coding agents.
items.why_included: A commenter said it met nearly all of their Markdown-editor wishlist and was easy to extend locally.
items.evidence: A commenter said Hubble had almost everything on their Markdown-editor wishlist and reported adding Mermaid rendering to a local build.

evidence_sources.author: shreddude
evidence_sources.excerpt: I’ve been waiting for an app like this to be developed!

items.name: Kimi K3-256k
items.summary: A Kimi coding model offering a 256k-token context window.
items.why_included: A long-term user endorsed its service recovery after demand surged following the K3 launch.
items.evidence: A commenter said they had used Kimi for months and were glad capacity was prioritized for existing customers after K3's launch.

evidence_sources.author: zorked
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have been using Kimi for months.
